## Problem

GitHub code scanning reports TWO OPEN high-severity alerts — the only open alerts on the repository:

    81  py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization  tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py:249  high
    82  py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization  tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py:250  high

Both are this pattern in `test_a_fallback_entry_endpoint_is_built_against_that_endpoint`:

    assert str(model.models[1].base_url).startswith("https://fallback.test")
    assert not str(model.models[0].base_url).startswith("https://fallback.test")

`startswith` on a URL is not a host check. `https://fallback.test.evil.example/` satisfies it, because
the attacker-controlled part sits AFTER the prefix the assertion pins. The rule is right about the
pattern.

## Honest severity assessment

CodeQL rates these high because the rule cannot distinguish test code from production code. In context
the exploitability is nil: the string is a hard-coded constant in a unit test, no untrusted input reaches
it, and nothing branches on the result except the assertion itself. So the real defect is not a
vulnerability — it is a WEAK ASSERTION. The test means "this model was built against that endpoint" but
checks "the base_url starts with these bytes", which would also pass for a different host sharing the
prefix. Fixing it makes the test say what it means AND clears the alert, so the two goals coincide and
there is no reason to dismiss instead.

Do NOT resolve this by dismissing the alerts, and do NOT add a suppression comment: the assertion
genuinely is weaker than intended.

## Approach

Compare the URL ORIGIN exactly rather than by prefix. Parse both sides with `urllib.parse.urlsplit` and
compare `(scheme, netloc)` as a tuple — exact equality has no substring semantics for CodeQL to flag and
no prefix ambiguity for a reader. `startswith` was presumably chosen because the client normalises the
configured endpoint (e.g. appends a trailing slash), which whole-string equality would break; comparing
the parsed origin keeps that tolerance without keeping the weakness.

Single-source the endpoint constant so the configured value and the asserted value cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Both assertions compare the parsed URL ORIGIN (scheme + host) by exact equality, and no
      `startswith`/`in` substring check against a URL remains anywhere in the file.
- [x] The test still FAILS if the fallback entry is built against the provider default instead of the
      configured endpoint — the property the test protects is preserved, verified by running it.
- [x] A host that merely shares the configured endpoint as a prefix
      (e.g. `https://fallback.test.evil.example`) does NOT satisfy the assertion, pinned by a test or by
      the construction of the comparison itself.
- [x] After the fix lands and CodeQL re-runs, `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/code-scanning/alerts` reports
      ZERO open `py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` alerts.
- [x] No alert is dismissed and no suppression comment is added — the code is changed.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
